# Report on `region.fasta` (`>region_012`)

**Overall:** 3,000 bp, single record, no ambiguity codes. Composition is AT/GC balanced overall (A 25.9%, C 28.0%, G 26.1%, T 20.0%; **GC = 54.1%**). This is not junk-like sequence — it is densely protein-coding, and several features stand out.

## 1. A sharp compositional discontinuity at ~position 790

Sliding-window GC content is flat at **~40–48% over positions 1–790** and jumps to **~57–60% over positions 791–3000** (45.2% vs 57.3% for the two halves; the transition occurs over ~30–50 bp, immediately at the gene boundary described below). Third-codon-position GC differs correspondingly between the genes (see below), so this looks like a genuine domain boundary rather than noise.

## 2. Three long, statistically significant open reading frames

| ORF | Strand | Coordinates (coding) | Start / stop | Length | Product character |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | + | **39–788** | ATG 39–41 / TAA 789–791 | 250 aa | soluble-ish; one C-terminal hydrophobic segment (aa 208–237 ≈ nt 660–749) |
| 2 | − | **1603–2592** | ATG 2590–2592 / TGA 1600–1602 | 330 aa | highly hydrophobic, polytopic membrane protein (≈9 predicted TM helices; e.g. nt ~1611–1765, 1791–1915, 1935–2020, 2091–2314, 2340–2413, 2496–2590) |
| 3 | − | **791–1744** | ATG 1742–1744 / TAA 788–790 | 318 aa | soluble; **ABC-transporter ATP-binding (nucleotide-binding) domain** |

Both long ORFs are stop-free over their entire length (0 stops in 318 and 330 codons respectively). In a random sequence of this composition the expected number of stop-free runs of ≥300 codons is ≈0.02, so these are almost certainly real coding sequences, not long chance ORFs. (ORF 3's frame shows GC3 ≈ 51%, ORF 2's ≈ 67%, ORF 1's ≈ 48% — all typical of coding DNA.)

## 3. Recognisable protein motifs (ORF 3, the 318-aa minus-strand protein)

This protein is an **ABC-type ATPase (nucleotide-binding domain)**, with the diagnostic elements:

- **Walker A / P-loop**, `GPNGCGKST`, aa 87–95 (≈ nt 1460–1486)
- **ABC signature motif**, `LSGGQ…` / `GQRQRAWI`, aa 191–201 (≈ nt 1150–1174)
- **Walker B**, `DEPTT`, aa 215–219 (≈ nt 1088–1102)
- Switch/H-loop region, `HLIAL…`, aa ~255–265

Its frequent membrane-protein partner is encoded immediately adjacent (ORF 2). Together ORF 3 + ORF 2 have the signature of an **ABC transporter operon** (permease + ATPase). The gene on the plus strand (ORF 1) has no matchable motif I can call from the sequence alone.

## 4. Two unusual arrangement features (the most notable findings)

**(a) Convergent genes with overlapping stop codons.** ORF 1 (plus strand) and ORF 3 (minus strand) both terminate at the same spot. Positions **788–791 read `TTAA`**, a 4-bp palindrome that supplies `TAA` on the plus strand (ORF 1 stop, 789–791) *and* `TAA` on the minus strand (ORF 3 stop, 788–790). So the two stop codons overlap by 2 bp.

**(b) An overlapping gene pair on the minus strand.** ORF 2 (1603–2592) and ORF 3 (791–1744) **overlap over positions 1603–1744 (142 bp ≈ 47 codons) in two different reading frames** (a 2-nt register shift). Both genes have their own ATG start and their own stop codon, and the overlapping segment is simultaneously stop-free in both frames. Because 318 + 330 codons = 1,944 bp of coding sequence are packed into just 1,802 bp of DNA (791–2592), the overlap is forced: this part of the region is **double-coded**. Overlapping same-strand genes are a hallmark of very compact genomes; note also that ORF 2's coding region is not free — its stop codon (1600–1602) lies *inside* the coding region of ORF 3.

## 5. Features that are *not* present (checked and negative)

- No exact repeated sequence ≥12 bp anywhere; no long inverted repeat (≥16 bp); no tandem/microsatellite repeats.
- No obvious canonical promoter (−35 `TTGACA` absent; a single `TATAAT` at 1990), no Shine–Dalgarno `AGGAGG`/`AAGGAG` upstream of any of the three ATGs, and no convincing rho-independent terminator (only a 6-T run at 1603, immediately 3′ of the ORF 2 stop).
- Homopolymer runs are short (max 6 nt); only 15 `GATC` (Dam) sites; no Chi sites; restriction sites are unremarkable (e.g. single NdeI at 2787, three EcoRV).

## Conclusions / caveats

Something clearly stands out: the region is essentially all coding, contains **three complete genes**, and exhibits a **compact, double-coded arrangement** — a convergent gene pair with overlapping (palindromic `TTAA`) stop codons, and **two overlapping minus-strand genes in different reading frames**, one of which encodes an ABC-transporter ATPase and the other a polytopic membrane protein (plausibly a transporter permease partner). There is also a sharp GC-content step (45% → 57%) at precisely the 788–791 gene boundary, which may mark a compositional/junctional boundary. The plus-strand gene's product (250 aa) is of unknown function from inspection alone.

Caveats: no database search was available here, so the functional assignments rest on sequence motifs only; coordinates are 1-based inclusive on the submitted plus strand; hydrophobicity/TM boundaries and motif nucleotide ranges are approximate (protein-level residue ranges are the more reliable figures).
